sections.heading: 1. Core Architecture & Mental Model of Introduction to Cybersecurity
sections.content: Cybersecurity operates under the principle of defense-in-depth and the CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability). In Introduction to Cybersecurity, defensive controls, least privilege, threat modeling, and telemetry monitoring prevent adversaries from gaining unauthorized footholds or escalating privileges.

codeExamples.code:
# Defensive Security & Telemetry Inspection for Introduction to Cybersecurity
# 1. Audit listening network sockets
sudo ss -tulpn

# 2. Inspect authentication failure anomalies in system logs
sudo grep -i "failed password" /var/log/auth.log | awk '{print $1, $2, $3, $11}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 10

# 3. Verify file permissions on critical system assets
sudo find /etc/shadow -perm /o+rwx
codeExamples.explanation: Auditing active listening ports and parsing authentication logs identifies unauthorized reconnaissance or intrusion attempts before exploitation occurs.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Summary list of top attacker source IP addresses attempting brute-force authentication.

keyPoints: Enforce the Principle of Least Privilege: users and processes receive only minimum necessary access.
Validate and sanitize all ingress data at service boundaries using parameterized constructs.
Log security events (authentication, privilege escalation, policy violations) centrally to an immutable SIEM.
commonMistakes: Relying on security through obscurity (such as changing a default port without hardening authentication).
Storing plain-text credentials or API tokens in source code or configuration files.

sections.heading: 2. Production Patterns & Real-World Implementations
sections.content: Modern security architectures adopt Zero Trust: verify explicitly, enforce least-privilege access, and assume breach across all network segments.

codeExamples.code:
# Zero-Trust Network Policy Example (iptables / UFW)
sudo ufw default deny incoming
sudo ufw default allow outgoing
sudo ufw allow from 10.0.10.0/24 to any port 22 proto tcp
sudo ufw enable
codeExamples.explanation: Default-deny network ingress policies isolate workloads so only authorized subnets and ports can establish connections.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Firewall active and enabled on system startup with default-deny inbound posture.

keyPoints: Validate assumptions at domain boundaries rather than assuming callers supply well-formed data.
Ensure operations and calculations are auditable, reproducible, and verifiable.
commonMistakes: Proceeding without clear acceptance criteria or error telemetry.
Silently ignoring failure modes instead of implementing deterministic error handling.

exercises.title: Security Case Study Lab: Introduction to Cybersecurity
exercises.objective: Diagnose a security vulnerability scenario and propose defense-in-depth mitigations.
exercises.description: Analyze the security incident scenario outlined in Introduction to Cybersecurity. Identify the threat vector, determine impacted CIA triad components, and define mitigation steps.
instructions: Classify the threat vector using STRIDE or MITRE ATT&CK categories.
Identify the root-cause vulnerability in configuration, code, or architecture.
Provide immediate containment steps and long-term preventive controls.
exercises.starterCode:
// Security Incident Analysis: Introduction to Cybersecurity
Incident Type: Unauthorized Access Attempt
Affected Asset: Production Database Ingress
Identified Vulnerability: Missing network ACL & weak credential policy
Proposed Containment:
1. Revoke compromised credentials immediately
2. Restrict IP ingress via security group
3. Rotate all dependent service secrets
hints: Consider both network layer and application layer controls.
Think about how authentication and authorization differ in this scenario.
exercises.submissionRequirements: Submit an actionable incident response summary with technical mitigation steps.
evaluationCriteria: Threat Understanding: Accurately identifies root cause and attack surface.
Mitigation Feasibility: Recommendations follow defense-in-depth principles without breaking legitimate services.
exercises.solutionExplanation: The optimal security response contains active exposure through immediate credential revocation and firewall isolation, followed by root-cause remediation (e.g. MFA enforcement and principle of least privilege).

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What is the foundational principle of a 'Zero Trust' security architecture?

options.text: Never trust, always verify: every access request must be authenticated, authorized, and encrypted regardless of network location.
Internal network requests behind a corporate VPN are automatically trusted.
Zero Trust means eliminating all user passwords in favor of IP address whitelisting alone.
Zero Trust applies exclusively to physical data center badge access.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Zero Trust assumes that threats exist both inside and outside the traditional network perimeter. Every request is explicitly verified, given least-privilege access, and assumed to operate in an untrusted environment.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Which of the following represent effective defense-in-depth controls against unauthorized access and data breaches?

options.text: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) on all administrative and corporate accounts
Centralized, tamper-evident audit logging sent to a SIEM
Disabling firewall rules to reduce network latency during high-load periods
Encrypting sensitive data both at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3)

knowledgeChecks.explanation: MFA, centralized logging, and end-to-end encryption are critical layers of defense in depth. Disabling firewall rules removes perimeter protection and exposes internal services to attack.

recap: In this lesson, you established the foundations of Introduction to Cybersecurity. You explored core architecture patterns, studied production resilience techniques, completed a hands-on exercise, and validated your understanding through knowledge checks.
